title: The Road to Reims
description: June-July 1429. After the victory at Orleans, Joan of Arc must escort the Dauphin Charles through English-held territory to the cathedral at Reims for his coronation. English garrisons at Troyes and Chalons block the route and can be fought or persuaded to surrender. Victory requires the Dauphin reaching Reims cathedral alive; his death means defeat.

anachronisms_found: BERSERK (Player THREE) as the 'raider chief' — a Viking unit roughly five centuries out of period and out of culture for 1429 Champagne; a Woad Raider-free engine still offers Two-Handed Swordsman, Brigand-style Militia-line upgrades, or Knights for a bandit chief
MILITIA x5 (Player THREE) — a Dark Age unit type; by 1429 the engine's Man-at-Arms/Long Swordsman or Spearman-line upgrades were the obvious available choices

English garrison armed with CROSSBOWMAN x6 instead of the engine's available Longbowman/Archer line — the longbow was the defining English weapon of the Hundred Years' War and its omission is entirely avoidable
Player TWO's MONASTERY placed inside the hostile Troyes/Chalons fortifications rather than a church/cathedral at the Reims goal, so the coronation site itself has no ecclesiastical building
TREE_OAK x2400 blanketing a 120x120 map — the Champagne route from Gien through Auxerre, Troyes and Chalons is open chalk farmland, not dense forest
